title: Multi-value --lora-path/--lora-scale produce a LIST that crashes when fed to scalar pipeline kwargs
detail: The CLI registers --lora-scale/--lora-path as repeated/multi flags (action=append-style), so args.lora_scale / args.lora_path arrive as a Python list. Several command modules pass this list straight into a scalar kwarg: profile hands args.lora_path to pipeline.generate(lora_path=...) (expects one path), faceswap wraps args.lora_scale into lora_scales=[lora_scale] producing a nested list [[...]], expansion assigns the whole list to scalar lora_scale, and workflow stuffs the list into RunConfig.lora_scale (a float dataclass field). All four are latent crashes that only fire when a user actually passes the flag along that code path — static checks miss them. Fix pattern: unwrap to a scalar at the boundary, or make the pipeline kwargs accept lists consistently. Found via effort:low review-only scan (4 of 13 findings).

title: A flag's required=True is NOT satisfied by its --alias when both share the same dest
detail: refine.py registers --input-image with required=True, then app/commands/_shared registers --input to the SAME dest (input_image). argparse only recognizes the original option string for the required check, so a caller using --input (the alias) is rejected as missing-required even though the value landed in the dest. Net effect: the --input alias is permanently unusable for refine. General rule: when aliasing an option via shared dest, set required=True on only ONE registration and never rely on an alias to satisfy a required flag. Found via effort:low review-only scan (2 of 13 findings, one scored high).

title: Frame-floor helpers that early-return on a mod predicate bypass the minimum-frames guarantee
detail: video-vbvr._adjust_frames returns frames=1 unchanged when (frames-1)%8==0 — the modulo predicate is satisfied by 1 (since 0%8==0), so the 9-frame minimum is silently bypassed for that input. Pattern: any floor/ceiling helper whose guard is a divisibility/mod check rather than a direct comparison (frames < MIN) can pass the boundary value straight through. Always express floors as explicit numeric comparisons, not as side-effects of a mod branch. Found via effort:low review-only scan (1 of 13, medium).

title: A ternary expression used as a bare statement discards its value — correctness depends on side-effect ordering
detail: video-relay uses `x if cond else y` as a standalone statement (not assigned). The ternary evaluates only one branch and throws the result away, so any code that relied on BOTH branches' side-effects (e.g. shutil.move ordering) is fragile. Linters rarely flag it because it is syntactically valid. Rewrite as an explicit if/else so the intended branch's side-effect is unambiguous. Found via effort:low review-only scan (1 of 13, low).

title: effort:low review-only scan surfaces genuine latent bugs with ~0 adversarial overturn
detail: Default cheap lane (lanes:[review,lint], fix.mode=review-only) reliably surfaces real latent bugs across runs. 2026-06-19 run: 13 findings, ALL 13 passed adversarial verification (0 overturned). 2026-06-20 run: 6 findings, adversarialUpheld=0 again. 2026-06-21 run: 9 findings, adversarialUpheld=0 AGAIN (1 high + 3 medium + 5 low; argparse-integrity(6) + correctness(2) + error-handling(1)). Takeaway: the low-effort review lane has a consistently high signal rate (≈0 adversarial overturn across THREE independent runs, 28 findings total); run it routinely and only escalate to medium+fix when you want changes applied. Adversarial-verify on effort:low is near-ceremony here — consider skipping it to cut cost on routine scans.

title: Findings cluster in command modules at the argparse→pipeline boundary (image-*, video-*, refine)
detail: All findings live in app/commands/ modules where argparse args (lists, required flags, defaults) meet pipeline dataclasses (scalars, fixed kwargs) — the type-coercion/dest-collision/default-bleed seam. 2026-06-19: 13/13 findings in app/commands/* (correctness + argparse-integrity), none in app/pipelines, app/workflows, or app/lib. 2026-06-20: 6/6 in app/commands/* (image-purify, image-review, video-relay, video-segment, animate). 2026-06-21: 9/9 in app/commands/* (image-t2i, image-profile, image-workflow, animate, video-restore, video-relay, video-segment). Review focus on app/commands/* yields the highest bug density for this codebase; the boundary between user-facing argparse and typed pipeline constructors is the dominant defect locus. Lint lane (pyflakes/check-model/self-test) stays clean on code quality (pyflakesRealCount=0, selftestOk=true across runs); checkModelOk=false is an infra/model-state signal, not a code defect.

title: A hardcoded pipeline kwarg (False/None) or an omitted kwarg silently freezes/forgets a feature even if a flag exists upstream
detail: Two faces of the same trap, both in video-relay. (1) Hardcoded literal: temporal_upscale=False is passed as a literal to LTXVideoPipeline — not sourced from any arg or default; no --temporal-upscale flag is registered on the relay parser, so the code path is permanently unreachable from the relay subcommand even though the underlying pipeline and the non-relay generate path support it. (2) Omitted kwargs: relay's pipeline.generate(...) call drops audio_stage1_only, audio_cfg_scale, modality_scale, audio_path, audio_volume — the args exist upstream (the generate path threads them) but the relay copy never passes them, so relay silently runs with pipeline defaults instead of the caller's audio/modality settings. General trap: any kwarg constructed as a bare literal in a command module, OR silently dropped from a copy-pasted generate() call, decouples the feature from the CLI surface — the flag can exist (or be assumed to exist) while the behavior is frozen/forgotten. Fix: thread the value from args (default it in the defaults table, register a flag), diff the kwargs against the canonical generate path, or delete the dead capability so the frozen-False/missing-kwarg is honest. Found via effort:low review-only scan (high + medium).

title: A flag registered in multiple sub-actions with differing intended defaults bleeds the first registration's default (first-writer-wins); a default=None sentinel is NOT safe either — it poisons the dest
detail: Image sub-actions each add their own --seed/--output via guarded _arg_registered checks, but the guard only prevents a *duplicate add* — it does NOT normalize the default to the caller's intent. Two failure modes: (1) image-purify registers --seed default=42 (SeedVR2 noise) while the canonical t2i seed default is 777; whichever sub-action's parser builds first wins, so a user can get seed=42 semantics instead of 777 when the shared args merge. Same class: image-review --output (unguarded add, semantic conflict with purify --output). (2) image-profile registers --seed with default=None as a sentinel — but because profile's parser is the FIRST/only writer on a shared dest across ALL image sub-actions on the unified parser, default=None leaks into every image sub-action's --seed, silently treating an explicit user --seed as None (i.e. the profile sentinel poisons the seed for t2i/faceswap/etc.). Trap: a guard that dedupes registration is not a guard that reconciles defaults; AND a None sentinel on a shared dest is just as destructive as a wrong concrete default, because downstream code branches on `is None`. When the same dest serves sub-actions with different default intents, resolve the value explicitly per sub-action at runtime from a fresh local (never store the sentinel in the shared dest); do not rely on registration order or on None-as-skip. Found via effort:low review-only scan (purify seed medium, image-review --output medium, image-profile --seed high).

title: Bare subprocess.run(...) without except FileNotFoundError / Timeout wraps a crash in an unhelpful traceback
detail: video-relay._extract_last_frame calls subprocess.run([ffmpeg,...]) with capture_output=True, timeout=60 but no try/except. If the ffmpeg binary is missing, Python raises FileNotFoundError deep in the subprocess call (not a clean 'ffmpeg not found' message); if it exceeds timeout it raises subprocess.TimeoutExpired. The code only checks result.returncode AFTER the call, so the exception type is never converted to a user-facing message. Pattern: any subprocess.run on a possibly-missing external binary (ffmpeg/ffprobe/CLI tool) must be wrapped — catch FileNotFoundError and emit a guided install hint, catch TimeoutExpired and degrade. The helper also has a fallback second subprocess.run with the same gap. Found via effort:low review-only scan (medium).

title: A handle released on the happy path (cap.release()) is leaked if any later line raises; try/finally is mandatory for cv2/file handles
detail: cv2.VideoCapture/VideoWriter (and any OS handle) opened then released only on the success path leaks the handle / leaves the file locked when any line between open and release raises. Confirmed across multiple command modules: video-segment opens VideoCapture, reads metadata, then calls cap.release() — but only on the success path; any exception between open and release (or in subsequent detect_scenes/scenes_to_timestamps calls that still reference the video) skips release(). video-restore opens BOTH cv2.VideoCapture and a VideoWriter without try/finally — a later exception leaks both handles. General trap: a happy-path release() is not resource safety. Prefer with/contextlib.closing (or try/finally) so the release is exception-safe. Found via effort:low review-only scan (video-segment low 2026-06-20; video-restore medium 2026-06-21).

title: A command module that fully implements the contract (PARSER_META/add_args/run) but is absent from COMMAND_NAMES is unreachable
detail: animate.py implements PARSER_META, add_args(parser), and run(args) — the full command module contract — yet 'animate' is NOT in cli.COMMAND_NAMES ([image, refine, upscale, caption, replay, video, import-lora, import-workflow, check-model, schema-defaults, schema]) nor in COMMAND_ALIASES. So build_parser never registers it, `run.py animate` is an unknown command, and the module is dead code that still type-checks as valid (no static analyzer flags it, because it is internally complete). Re-flagged TWO findings in the 2026-06-21 run (a low and a medium, both naming animate.py) — the orphan persists across runs, confirming it was not fixed. Trap: a module can pass every quality gate while being structurally unreachable. Guard: assert the module's name appears in COMMAND_NAMES (a one-line integrity test), or delete the stub. The repo already has test_selftest_integrity.py for a parallel case (deleted-test references); a COMMAND_NAMES-membership assertion is the analog fix. Found via effort:low review-only scan (low 2026-06-20; low+medium 2026-06-21).

title: Help text that advertises a default the argparse default doesn't match, or a duplicate flag whose guarded twin is silently skipped, misleads users and reviewers
detail: Two related argparse-integrity gaps surfaced in the 2026-06-21 run. (1) Stale advertised default: image-t2i's help string advertises default 640/960, but the argparse default is None (the sentinel pattern) — a user reading --help is told a value is preset when it is not, and a reviewer reading help text cannot trust it as the source of truth. (2) Guarded-twin divergence: image-workflow registers --film-grain / --sharpening WITHOUT the _arg_registered guard, while image-purify registers guarded copies of the same flags — the guard dedupes and silently keeps only the FIRST (purify's) registration, so the workflow-specific help text/defaults never take effect even though they look wired. The two are the same root cause: the help/default surface and the actual argparse registration surface have drifted apart, and nothing asserts they agree. Fix: treat help text as a contract — add an integrity test that parses --help and asserts each flag's advertised default equals argparse's actual default; and for shared flags, register in exactly ONE place (canonical t2i/_shared) and never re-add unguarded in a sub-action. Found via effort:low review-only scan (image-t2i low, image-workflow low).
